pages.text: $(bold)Description:$() The macroscopic expression of defocus is the substitution of form: the semantics of one object are replaced by another set of semantics, and its material composition changes accordingly. There is no observable causal link between the replacement and the original object, and no conservation of mass, volume or function.

Substitution occurs at the object level. No case of sub-object defocus has ever been recorded, and no products such as black holes or antimatter have been recorded either. The previous observer's explanation for this class of case was "out of scope".$(br2)We have never been able to confirm what that means.

$(bold)Stage characteristics:$() Defocus does not spread at a constant rate. As the iteration advances it intensifies in three ways at once:$(br2)$(li)$(l)Frequency$(): the interval before the same object drifts again shortens with each stage;$(br)$(li)$(l)Probability$(): the chance of a drift occurring in a single settlement rises with each stage;$(br)$(li)$(l)Scope$(): the kinds of object affected widen with each stage.
All three can be inspected live in the field interface.$(br2)The only certainty is direction: it will only get faster, and it will not slow down on its own.
